In this section, we conduct an in-depth investigation of the three research questions (RQs) introduced in the Section 1 through experiments on English-Chinese translation.

Evaluation and Training. All our experiments were run using $1 ~ \times$ NVIDIA V100 32G, for different LLM variants. We use vLLM& (Kwon et al., 2023) to save inference time.We keep the parameters consistent with those used in previous work (Qian et al., 2O24). For training,we use the Qwen2.5-7B as base model for supervised fine-tuning base on the LLaMAFactory framework9.The Details of the training procedure parameters are provided in Appendix A.

Evaluation Data. As shown in Table 1, the training and testing data sizes for the English-Chinese and German-English datasets are presented. Besides these two language pairs, we use data sets from FLORES10 (NLLB Team et al., 2024), selecting Japanese-English and Korean-English. The test set consists of 1,O12 sentences covering three domains: Wikinews,Wikibooks,and Wikiyago,referred to in paper as the news,book,and travel domains. After domain-wise splitting, the data for these three domains consist of 341, 351, and 321 sentences, respectively. Additionally, regarding the scoring of alignment quality, we observe that our human annotated results achieve higher accuracy,as shown in Table 10.

Specifically, we chose the default hyperparameter settings in vLLM for all our experiments, i.e., 0.8 as temperature 4, O.95 for top_p. The input sequence length was chosen as 1O24 for zero-shot and CoT inference and 3ooO for few-shot inference.For the training procedure, we utilize the LoRA (Hu et al., 2021) to fine-tune the Qwen-2.5-7B. The hyperparameters for supervised fine-tuning are listed in Table 9.
